items.title: Wei-Mi-Shu Decoction ameliorates gastric mucosal injury in chronic gastritis with liver-stomach disharmony syndrome through the gut microbiota-hepatic bile acid metabolism axis.
items.abstract: Chronic gastritis (CG) is a high-incidence disease in the digestive system, and liverstomach disharmony syndrome (LSD) is a relatively common syndrome type. This study aimed to evaluate the role and possible mechanism of traditional Chinese medicine Wei-Mi-Shu Decoction (WMS) in treating LSDCG. The CG and LSDCG animal models were established and treated with WMS to observe the TCM syndrome scores and behavioral changes, histopathological alterations of the gastric mucosa, and expressions of pro-inflammatory cytokines and tight junction proteins. Then, the changes of gut microbiota and bile acids (BAs) were analyzed by microbiota sequencing and mass spectrometry, and the protein expressions of BA receptors were detected by immunohistochemistry and WB. Finally, Lgr5-positive (Lgr5 + ) gastric cells were observed by immunofluorescence staining, the expression of gastric mucosal cell differentiation markers was detected by RT-qPCR, and the fatty acid oxidation (FAO) of Lgr5 + cells was observed by fluorescence double staining. WMS reduced the TCM syndrome scores, increased the autonomous activity ability, and improved gastric mucosal injury, inflammatory response, and gastric mucosal barrier disruption in the CG and LSDCG model rats. WMS also regulated the intestinal microbiota and BA metabolism of model rats, and promoted the levels of PPARα and RXR. In addition, WMS attenuated the loss of Lgr5 + gastric stem cells and promoted their differentiation and FAO. In conclusion, WMS promoted the differentiation of Lgr5 + gastric stem cells, potentially involving the gut microbiotahepatic BA metabolism axis to repair gastric mucosal injury in LSDCG.

items.title: Bilateral renal infarction unmasking rheumatic mitral valve disease with left atrial appendage thrombus in sinus rhythm: a case report.
items.abstract: Acute renal infarction mimics pyelonephritis and is frequently missed at first presentation. Rheumatic mitral stenosis can cause systemic embolism even in sinus rhythm. A 47-year-old Thai man presented with four days of evolving abdominal pain, previously attributed to gastroenteritis and treated symptomatically at a first emergency visit. He had fever without chills, left costovertebral-angle tenderness, and a bland urinalysis. Point-of-care ultrasound was atypical for pyelonephritis; computed tomography showed bilateral wedge-shaped cortical defects with a cortical rim sign but could not exclude focal bacterial nephritis. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound demonstrated an avascular left upper pole, confirming bland infarction, supported by lactate dehydrogenase 1194 U/L, procalcitonin 0.28 ng/mL, and sterile cultures. Echocardiography revealed rheumatic mitral valve disease with clinically significant stenosis (valve area 1.34 cm 2 by planimetry; diastolic doming, commissural fusion, fish-mouth orifice) and moderate regurgitation. The left atrium was dilated, with dense spontaneous echo contrast and a left atrial appendage thrombus despite sinus rhythm. Enoxaparin with overlapping warfarin was started; a direct oral anticoagulant was avoided. At 2 months the patient was in New York Heart Association class II without recurrent embolism, but the international normalized ratio had not yet reached target; repeat transoesophageal echocardiography is scheduled at 3 months. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound can resolve the computed tomography ambiguity between infarction and focal bacterial nephritis at the bedside. In mitral stenosis, a prior embolic event or left atrial thrombus mandates vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation irrespective of rhythm, and an appendage thrombus and coexisting mitral regurgitation defer balloon commissurotomy.

items.title: Short-term decongestion and clinical benefit in acute heart failure: a systematic review and trial-level meta-regression.
items.abstract: Body weight, urine output, urinary sodium, and ultrasound findings are frequently used as early trial endpoints in acute heart failure (AHF). However, patient-level prognostic associations with residual congestion do not establish the fact that treatment-induced marker improvement predicts fewer deaths or heart failure events. The objectives of this work are to pair short-term decongestion and subsequent clinical treatment effects within the same randomized comparisons, explore the trial-level association for body weight, and qualitatively assess non-weight markers. PubMed/MEDLINE, OpenAlex, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases were searched through 18 July 2026. Eligible randomized adult AHF trials reported an objective decongestion effect and ≥30-day mortality, heart failure events, or rehospitalization. The amended primary marker was weight change at 24-96 h (original window, 48-96 h); clinical effects were log hazard or risk ratios. An errors-in-variables meta-regression model used 10,000 trial cluster bootstrap fits and trial-level jackknife intervals. Twenty-four trials (27 reports) were accepted for qualitative synthesis; the primary analysis included 12 comparisons from only 10 independent trials. Endpoints, follow-up (30-302 days), effect measures, and mechanisms were heterogeneous. Each additional 1-kg between-group difference in weight loss corresponded to a clinical effect ratio of 0.74 (percentile 95% interval, 0.56-1.26; jackknife, 0.49-1.11). The pharmacological-only estimate was 1.04. Evidence for urine output, urinary sodium, and ultrasound was also inconsistent. Short-term weight loss showed a directional but non-robust trial-level association with clinical benefit. The randomized trial-level evidence evaluated here is insufficient to validate short-term weight change as a surrogate for post-discharge clinical outcomes in AHF.

items.title: Effects of mindfulness-based interventions on negative emotions in patients with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Psychological distress is common in hypertension and may impair disease management. Mindfulness-based interventions have been proposed to improve emotional and health-related outcomes, but evidence in this population remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched up to December 31, 2025, for randomized controlled trials of mindfulness interventions in adults with hypertension. Continuous outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using fixed- or random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. Nine trials with 780 participants were included. Mindfulness interventions significantly reduced depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.19, 95% CI: -1.74 to -0.64) and anxiety (SMD = -1.43, 95% CI: -2.48 to -0.39). Perceived stress was also reduced (SMD = -0.53, 95% CI: -0.82 to -0.24). Systolic (SMD = -2.10, 95% CI: -3.81 to -0.38) and diastolic blood pressure (SMD = -1.55, 95% CI: -2.69 to -0.42) were modestly reduced. Risk of bias was generally low to moderate. According to GRADE, the certainty of evidence was moderate for depression, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and low for anxiety, perceived stress, and quality of life. Mindfulness-based interventions improve psychological outcomes in hypertension and may modestly lower blood pressure, supporting their use as a complementary strategy in hypertension management. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, PROSPERO CRD420261328666.

items.title: Familial severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with coexisting likely pathogenic BAG3 and FLNC variants: a case report.
items.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is genetically heterogeneous. In severe non-ischemic DCM with familial clustering of heart-failure deaths, genetic testing and pedigree analysis may clarify etiology and guide cascade screening. A 40-year-old woman presented with progressive dyspnea, chest tightness, and palpitations after an upper respiratory tract infection. Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) approximately 20%], left atrial enlargement, functional mitral regurgitation, and a small pericardial effusion. Serial cardiac troponin I and myocardial enzyme measurements remained within the reference ranges. Coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary disease. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) demonstrated global left ventricular hypokinesis and a clinically reported non-ischemic late-gadolinium-enhancement pattern at the papillary-muscle level involving the anterior/lateral wall. Because cardiac biomarkers remained normal and dedicated inflammatory CMR sequences were not acquired, active myocarditis could not be confirmed. Guideline-directed therapy reduced NT-proBNP from 4154 to 828 pg/mL, although angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy was limited by symptomatic hypotension. At 2 months, symptoms and daily activity tolerance improved, but LVEF remained 25%, QTc was 479 ms, and ventricular premature complexes persisted. Whole-exome sequencing identified heterozygous likely pathogenic variants in BAG3 (NM_004281.4:c.180 + 1G > T) and FLNC [NM_001458.5:c.761_779del, p.(Leu254Profs*14)]. The daughter carried the BAG3 variant, whereas both children were negative for FLNC. The proband reported heart-failure-related deaths in her father and younger brother during adulthood and in a nephew during childhood. The findings support complex familial non-ischemic DCM with marked variable expressivity. Coexisting BAG3 and FLNC variants should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than proof of dual-gene causality. The infection-associated acute decompensation, persistently normal cardiac injury biomarkers, non-ischemic LGE, and incomplete inflammatory CMR characterization favor cautious interpretation rather than a definitive diagnosis of myocarditis. Serial imaging, rhythm surveillance, individualized device-risk assessment, and follow-up of genotype-positive relatives are essential.

items.title: An immune-resistance dual-axis framework prioritizes MAL2 for functional investigation in lung cancer.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped lung cancer treatment, yet durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients. Biomarkers incompletely capture interactions between immune activation and tumor-intrinsic resistance. Integrating immune and epithelial expression programs may help identify response-associated states and candidates for functional investigation. Public bulk transcriptomes were analyzed with format-specific preprocessing, empirical Bayes differential expression, standardized cross-cohort evidence, and gene-set enrichment. Five discovery-informed modules formed an immune-resistance score. Conditional leave-one-out and leave-cohort-out analyses refitted normalization within training data and compared the fixed score with a nested ridge-logistic model. Survival, composition-adjustment, and prioritization sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell counts underwent quality control, unsupervised clustering, and patient-level pseudobulk analysis. MAL2 was investigated in A549 and H1299 cells using knockdown, growth, motility, apoptosis, HLA-ABC, cytokine, and PBMC co-culture assays. No individual gene met FDR <0.05 in any of the three discovery contrasts. Favorable-response genes were enriched for adaptive immune processes, whereas the unfavorable list showed weaker DNA-replication enrichment. Conditional leave-cohort-out AUCs for the dual-axis score were 0.964, 0.859, and 0.773; performance did not consistently exceed the immune axis. In GSE190266, outcome analysis yielded a cohort-relative AUC of 0.617 with incomplete module coverage. Higher scores were associated with longer PFS in two evaluated cohorts. Quality control retained 91,762 single cells. MAL2 remained epithelial-enriched and ranked third among 58 evaluable candidates, but its patient-level epithelial response contrast and standalone PFS associations were not significant. Knockdown reduced growth and motility-related readouts, increased apoptosis and HLA-ABC expression, and altered cytokine and co-culture activation readouts. The immune-resistance framework links cohort-level response patterns to epithelial candidates for functional investigation. MAL2 depletion alters growth and immune-related phenotypes in lung cancer cells, supporting further investigation of its biological role.

items.title: Central nervous system involvement in relapsing polychondritis with inflammatory changes in the cerebrospinal fluid and cranial MRI abnormalities: a case series report.
items.abstract: To explore the clinical features of relapsing polychondritis (RP) with central nervous system (CNS) involvement as the major manifestation. A total of 11 RP patients who were hospitalized in the Department of Neurology, the Affiliated Brain Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2020 to December 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. Their clinical manifestations, laboratory indicators, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) changes, and cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings were comprehensively analyzed. CNS involvement was the major initial manifestation in the vast majority of RP patients (90.9%, 10/11), as cognitive impairment ( n  = 10), headache ( n  = 7), psychiatric/behavioral symptoms ( n  = 6), epileptic seizures ( n  = 4), limb numbness ( n  = 4), limb weakness ( n  = 4), and limb tremor ( n  = 3). CSF analysis revealed an inflammatory response in the CNS, as evidenced by increased levels of neutrophils, albumin, and immunoglobulins at varying degrees. White matter degeneration ( n  = 7) and brain atrophy ( n  = 7) were the pronounced changes on cranial MRI. Brain lesions were mainly distributed in the cortex, subcortex, and infratentorium. Parenchymal or meningeal enhancement was observed on MRI scans in three RP patients with CNS involvement. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) detected three cases of hypoperfusion and two cases of hyperperfusion in the brain. All patients were treated with corticosteroids, and six were managed with additional immunotherapies. Finally, ten RP patients were improved and discharged. neurological deficits vary widely in RP patients with CNS involvement, with cognitive decline as the most common feature. Inflammatory changes in the CSF indicate a neuroinflammatory mechanism involved in the pathogenesis of RP. Distinct imaging features on cranial MRI are closely associated with the involvement into CNS in RP, offering references for distinguishing the acute inflammation stage from the chronic degeneration stage during the development of RP.

items.title: COL1A2 expression is associated with prognosis, stromal remodeling, and predicted immunotherapy response in gastric cancer.
items.abstract: COL1A2 encodes type I collagen alpha2 chain, a stromal component in gastric cancer (GC); its prognostic value, cellular origin, and immune microenvironment relation remain unclear. We analyzed TCGA-STAD, GSE63089, and ACRG GSE62254. Associations between COL1A2 abundance and overall survival (OS), clinicopathology, pathways, and tumor microenvironment were assessed. High/low groups by median expression. Two Cox models used pathological stage or separate T/N/M. Immunotherapy response predicted via TIDE and IPS. WGCNA, PPI, and LASSO with five ECM genes, ten-fold cross-validation and 200 repeats, were applied. qPCR and Western blot measured mRNA and protein in seven paired tissues. COL1A2 was higher in GC and linked to poorer OS, but time-dependent AUCs were 0.60, 0.65, 0.66. In ACRG, OS association was not significant (HR 1.83, P = 0.085). Per SD increase, adjusted HR was 1.21 (stage model, P = 0.036) and 1.14 (T/N/M model, P = 0.171). C-index gains were only 0.006 and 0.003. Higher abundance correlated with stroma-rich microenvironment and M2 macrophage infiltration. TIDE/IPS predicted lower ICI response probability. LASSO selected SPARC, ELN, and BGN stably. Tumor tissues showed higher mRNA and protein. COL1A2 associates with poor prognosis, stromal remodeling, and predicted immunotherapy response, but its prognostic effect varies between models and discrimination improvement is small.

items.title: Genomic characteristics and preliminary study on in vitro infection properties of canine parvovirus type 2c derived from a canine anal swab sample.
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the genomic characteristics and genotype of a CPV isolate (MDC-CPV) recovered from a vaccinated dog, and to investigate its in vitro infectivity and replication features in A72 and CRFK cell lines. Clinical samples were subjected to nucleic acid detection for common canine pathogens and CPV antigen testing. Sequencing was performed using the Illumina NovaSeq PE150 platform. Following quality control, assembly, and annotation, the near-complete genome sequence of MDC-CPV was obtained. Homology searches were conducted using BLASTn. Genotyping was determined based on key amino acid residues in VP2, and phylogenetic analyses were performed using both the full-length VP2 coding sequence (CDS) and the whole-genome reference sequences. In vitro infection was subsequently validated in A72 and CRFK cells. Viral infection-associated characteristics were evaluated by observing cytopathic effects (CPE), and through Western blot, immunofluorescence, qPCR, TCID50 assay, and transmission electron microscopy. The genome length of MDC-CPV was 5,358 nucleotides, with no ambiguous bases identified. Genome annotation revealed that MDC-CPV contains typical CPV coding regions, including NS1, NS2, VP1, and VP2. The VP2 CDS was 1755 nucleotides in length, encoding 584 amino acids. Key VP2 residues for MDC-CPV were 297Ala/426Glu, along with a combination of other residues (87Leu, 101Thr, 300Gly, 305Tyr, 324Ile, 375Asp, 555Val, 564Ser, and 568Gly), supporting its classification as CPV-2c. Phylogenetic analysis placed MDC-CPV within the CPV-2c clade, showing close genetic relatedness to several CPV-2c reference strains from China and other regions in East Asia. In in vitro infection assays, CPE was observed in both A72 and CRFK cells inoculated with MDC-CPV. Furthermore, CPV-related protein expression and virus-like particles were detected. Quantitative PCR and TCID50 assays in CRFK cells demonstrated productive replication, with viral DNA levels and infectious virus titers increasing substantially from 48 h post-infection, reaching peak titers of approximately 5.8 log10 TCID50/1 mL at 96 h post-infection. MDC-CPV is a CPV-2c strain isolated from a clinical sample of a vaccinated dog. Its genomic and VP2 genotypic characteristics are consistent with recently circulating CPV-2c strains. These findings provide a reference for molecular epidemiological surveillance of CPV-2c in the Sichuan region and for research on CPV infection in the context of vaccination.

items.title: Case Report: Diverse clinical phenotypes and treatment responses in pediatric autoimmune nodopathy: a case series.
items.abstract: Autoimmune nodopathy (AN) is a recently identified category of immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy defined by circulating auto-antibodies against nodal and paranodal cell-adhesion molecules. We retrospectively reviewed three pediatric patients with antibody-positive AN diagnosed by cell-based assay (CBA). Three male patients aged 5 years 7 months to 13 years 8 months were positive for anti-NF186 (1:32), anti-Caspr1 (1:10), and anti-NF155 (1:100) IgG, respectively. The anti-NF186-positive patient and the anti-Caspr1-positive patient presented with a CIDP/GBS-like phenotype, whereas the anti-NF155-positive patient presented with tremor, sensory ataxia, and limb weakness resembling the adult AN phenotype. These patients also had markedly elevated CSF protein and electrophysiological findings of reduced or unobtainable CMAP and SNAP amplitudes; in addition, the NF155-positive patient showed slowed motor conduction velocity. All patients received first-line therapy with IVIG and intravenous methylprednisolone pulses followed by an oral prednisone taper. Two patients responded to this regimen, and the NF155-positive patient was refractory to first-line therapy but improved after rituximab. In this small series, pediatric AN is heterogeneous, and antibody subtyping with clinical assessment is essential for diagnosis. First-line immunotherapy was effective in NF186- and Caspr1-positive patients, whereas the NF155-positive patient improved only after adding rituximab. Early recognition, prompt diagnosis, and timely therapeutic intervention are of paramount importance for improving the prognosis of pediatric AN.

items.title: How men who have sex with men communicate about PrEP within interpersonal relationships: a qualitative analysis of data from the PROUD PrEP Study.
items.abstract: Use of oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) is crucial for preventing HIV and ending global transmission. This qualitative study focuses on behavioural factors surrounding PrEP, exploring how early UK PrEP users from the PROUD study communicated about PrEP within interpersonal relationships. Between February 2014 and January 2016, in-depth interviews were conducted with purposefully sampled PROUD participants. Interviews explored context surrounding PrEP communication and were analysed using thematic analysis. Forty-one participants were interviewed. PrEP use was discussed within a range of interpersonal relationships, but most often with other GBMSM. Communication was primarily motivated by educating friends and social networks about PrEP and navigating sex and relationships with partners. Participants received varied responses towards their PrEP use, with most resistance coming from GBMSM communities. Social attitudes signalled a lack of awareness about PrEP, stigma towards PrEP users, and framing of condomless sex as taboo. Findings highlight the need for social support interventions to facilitate PrEP communication and leverage social networks for information-sharing. Additionally, PrEP stigma must be addressed with public advocacy and awareness-raising. This study can inform the optimisation of PrEP programmes and the implementation of novel HIV and STI prevention modalities.

items.title: Medicinal Resins of Socotra: Phytochemical Diversity, Biological Activities, Safety, and Evidence Gaps.
items.abstract: Socotra (Yemen) is home to several resin-producing plant groups. This review evaluates the phytochemistry, biological activities, and safety of Dracaena cinnabari , Socotran Boswellia , and Commiphora resins, identifies gaps in the available evidence, and distinguishes resin-derived findings from bark-derived evidence. D. cinnabari resin contains homoisoflavans and chalcones, but quantitative data for major phenolics remain insufficient. Resin preparations showed antifungal and radical-scavenging activity in vitro; a resin extract and two chalcone derivatives reduced hepatitis B virus antigen production in culture without establishing antiviral efficacy. A methanolic resin extract was cytotoxic to six oral squamous cell carcinoma lines (half-maximal inhibitory concentration [IC 50 ]: 5.9-19.2 µg/mL). Two rat carcinogenesis protocols reported 14.3% carcinoma incidence at 1000 mg/kg versus 85.7% in carcinogen-only controls. A single study of acute and 28-day oral toxicity provides limited, extract-specific safety data. Boswellia and Commiphora resin chemistry is documented mainly through volatile profiles. B. elongata resin yielded 21 compounds, including boswellic acids, whose presence does not establish pharmacological equivalence to B. serrata or B. sacra ; four triterpenoid acids inhibited yeast α-glucosidase (IC 50 9.9-56.8 µM), but antidiabetic efficacy was not tested. Most other Boswellia bioactivity data concern bark. (+)-Yangambin accounted for 3.50-9.05% ( w / w ) of recovered C. ornifolia ethanol extracts. No eligible bioassays of Commiphora resins or human studies were identified. The evidence does not support therapeutic claims.

items.title: National Health Insurance Expenditure and Health-System Use for Hepatitis B and C in Bulgaria, 2021-2025.
items.abstract: National reimbursement records complement model-based estimates of hepatitis treatment costs. Our primary objective was to quantify Bulgarian National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) antiviral reimbursement and its price and quantity components; secondary objectives were to estimate dispensing-based treatment volume and describe service activity. This retrospective study analysed aggregated national pharmacy records for complete years 2021-2025 and hospital and outpatient records for complete years 2024-2025. Diagnosis-identified records were combined with product-identified antiviral prescriptions under fibrosis or cirrhosis codes. Fisher indices decomposed expenditure; seasonal quasi-Poisson models with Newey-West standard errors described monthly trends. Antiviral reimbursement totalled EUR 101.5 million, including EUR 91.6 million for HCV and EUR 10.0 million for HBV. Annual antiviral reimbursement increased from EUR 18.9 million to EUR 21.7 million. The budget share for all pharmacy products in the hepatitis case definition, including adjunctive products, declined from 3.99% to 2.61%. Relative to 2021, the 2025 Fisher price and quantity indices were 0.799 and 1.395 for HBV and 0.885 and 1.447 for HCV. Estimated mean continuous HBV therapy increased from 2226 to 3051 people; HCV standard-course equivalents increased from 604 to 777, with duration-based ranges of 431-607 and 571-777. These estimates do not identify unique treated patients. Annualised inpatient-episode trends during 2024-2025 were 9.2% for HBV and -7.4% for HCV; consultation trends were 3.7% and -6.9%. Dispensed treatment volume increased while reimbursed unit prices and the hepatitis pharmaceutical budget share declined. These findings describe payer expenditure and encounters; they do not establish improved affordability, access, or treatment coverage.

items.title: Paradoxical Splenic Signal Loss on Chemical-Shift MRI in Acute Toxic Hepatitis After Occupational Petroleum Sludge Exposure: A Case Series.
items.abstract: Background: Acute toxic hepatitis after work-related exposure to petroleum products is rare. Its imaging features are not well known. Methods: Seven men aged 18-35 years cleaned the same petroleum storage tank for two days. Symptoms began about 5 days later. Ultrasound and CT were done at admission. Non-contrast 3 T MRI with in-phase and opposed-phase imaging was done about 10 days after exposure. The splenic signal intensity ratio (SIR, in-phase/opposed-phase) was compared with that of 15 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Results: At admission, median ALT was 481 U/L, median AST 227 U/L, and median total bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL. The injury was hepatocellular by R ratio in the six patients with raised ALT. Periportal edema was seen in 6 of 7 patients. No patient had biliary obstruction or vascular thrombosis. Notably, all seven patients demonstrated paradoxical splenic signal loss on in-phase compared with opposed-phase MRI, with a median splenic signal intensity ratio (SIR) of 0.77 (IQR, 0.74-0.81; range, 0.70-0.87). Splenic SIR was lower in patients than in healthy controls (median 0.77 vs. 1.05; p Conclusions: In this single exposure cluster, the spleen lost signal on in-phase images. This pattern is usually linked to iron or other T2* effects. The finding is preliminary. It needs confirmation with iron measurement, hemolysis tests, and follow-up MRI.

items.title: Overt and Occult Hepatitis B in Hemodialysis Patients: Insights from High-Sensitivity Testing and Genetic Analysis.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Occult hepatitis B infection (OBI) remains a diagnostic challenge, particularly in hemodialysis (HD) patients, who are vulnerable to HBV infection due to immune dysfunction and repeated exposure. Methods: We evaluated the prevalence and molecular characteristics of OBI among 874 HD patients in St. Petersburg, Russia, using high-sensitivity nested real-time PCR targeting the S and X genes. Results: HBV DNA was detected in 3.7% (32/874), as reflected in subcategories: overt CHB in 2.1% (18/874) and OBI in 1.6% (14/874). Genotype D predominated (93.8%), with subgenotypes D2 (56.3%), D1 (25.0%), and D3 (12.5%) present. OBI patients had low viral loads (6.0-148.3 IU/mL), whereas CHB patients showed high viremia (7843-64,870,000 IU/mL). Immune escape mutations were significantly more frequent in OBI (92.9%) than CHB (16.7%; p p p = 0.0001). Conclusions: In conclusion, OBI affects 1.6% of HD patients in this cohort, with immune escape mutations as a key molecular driver of the occult phenotype. These findings suggest that HBV DNA screening may warrant consideration in HD patients, as serological results alone are inadequate for ruling out occult infection.

items.title: A highly successful case report: a patient with intestinal hepatoid adenocarcinoma and liver metastases achieves excellent efficacy following immune-targeted therapy.
items.abstract: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma (HAC) is a rare extrahepatic adenocarcinoma producing alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), with clinicopathological features resembling hepatocellular carcinoma, including aggressive behavior, poor prognosis, vascular invasion, and distant metastasis. It occurs mostly in the stomach and rarely in the colon. Due to its rarity, large randomized trials are lacking; thus, case reports provide valuable treatment information. Here, we report a 62-year-old woman initially diagnosed with massive hepatocellular carcinoma by computed tomography (CT) who underwent radical hepatectomy. Postoperative follow-up CT revealed lesions in the sigmoid colon and residual liver. Colonoscopic biopsy showed poorly differentiated carcinoma (adenocarcinoma with enteroblastic differentiation/hepatoid adenocarcinoma). She then received CAPOX (oxaliplatin plus capecitabine) combined with sintilimab and bevacizumab. After one year, follow-up imaging showed complete disappearance of the liver tumor and reduction of the sigmoid colon lesion. The final efficacy assessment was complete remission (CR) of the liver lesion and stable disease (SD) of the sigmoid colon lesion. This case report suggests that combined immune-targeted therapy and chemotherapy achieved excellent efficacy in a patient with intestinal hepatoid adenocarcinoma and liver metastases, and this combination regimen may provide a new treatment strategy for intestinal hepatoid adenocarcinoma (IHA).

items.title: Apoptosis-Inducing and Cytotoxic Effects of the Daphne mucronata Extract and Its Bioactive Compound Gnidilatimonoein in Liver Cancer Cells.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) continues to rank among the leading causes of cancer-related death worldwide, and the modest efficacy together with the systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapeutic regimens continues to constrain treatment outcomes. Identifying safer, more selective anticancer agents therefore remains a priority in toxicological and pharmacological research. Daphne mucronata, a medicinal plant native to Iran, has previously demonstrated anti-inflammatory and cytotoxic properties, yet the anticancer potential of the plant and its bioactive constituents in liver cancer has not been thoroughly characterized. In the present study, we examined the anticancer activity of D. mucronata extract and its purified diterpenoid constituent, gnidilatimonoein (GND), using HCC models. GND was isolated through column chromatography and further purified by high-performance liquid chromatography. Cytotoxicity and IC 50 values were determined in human HepG 2 and murine Hepa1-6 liver cancer cell lines, as well as normal human hepatocytes (THLE-2), using the MTT assay. Apoptotic activity was evaluated through annexin V/PI flow cytometry, caspase-3 activity assays, nitric oxide (NO) measurement, liver enzyme profiling, and Western blot analysis of Bax, Bcl-2, P53, and caspase-3 expression. Both the crude extract and purified GND significantly suppressed cancer cell proliferation in a dose-dependent manner (p 50 values of 1.36 mg/mL (HepG 2 ) and 1.23 mg/mL (Hepa1-6) for the extract, and 3.439 μg/mL (HepG 2 ) and 34.23 ng/mL (Hepa1-6) for GND. Notably, GND exhibited pronounced selectivity for malignant cells over normal hepatocytes and showed changes in apoptosis-related protein expression (elevated Bax, P53, and caspase-3, and decreased Bcl-2) consistent with engagement of the intrinsic mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Together, these findings position GND as a promising plant-derived candidate for HCC therapy, warranting further investigation into its in vivo efficacy and translational potential.

items.title: Clinical Management and Molecular Landscape of Combined Hepatocellular-Cholangiocarcinoma: A Comprehensive Review.
items.abstract: Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC-CCA) is a rare and highly aggressive primary liver cancer. It is distinguished by the unequivocal coexistence of both hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) components within a single tumor. cHCC-CCA accounts for between 0.4% and 14.2% of primary liver cancers, presenting a complex clinical and pathological challenge because of its dual histological morphology and phenotypic diversity. In the past, its classification faced significant diagnostic challenges. However, these issues have been largely addressed by the 2019 World Health Organization 5th Edition reclassification, which requires clear differentiation of hepatocytic and cholangiocytic features using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. Recent genomic profiling has shown that cHCC-CCA exists on a molecular spectrum, with about 75% of individual tumors being HCC-like or CCA-like. Biliary-dominant subtypes, similar to CCA, often contain actionable alterations like FGFR2 fusions, IDH1 mutations, and HER2 amplification, providing significant opportunities for precision oncology. In contrast, subtypes resembling HCC are commonly driven by mutations in TP53 and the TERT promoter. Major hepatectomy combined with regional lymphadenectomy continues to be a fundamental curative treatment. However, liver transplantation is increasingly being recognized as a viable option for carefully selected patients with early-stage cirrhosis. In the advanced or recurrent stage, the traditional preferred treatment continues to be cytotoxic gemcitabine combined with platinum-based therapies. Meanwhile, combinations involving immune checkpoint inhibitors, like atezolizumab and bevacizumab, or more complex regimens that integrate locoregional therapy, TKIs, and PD-(L)1 inhibitors, offer hopeful prospects for improving survival rates. This review provided an overview of the current knowledge of the clinical classification, risk stratification, histogenesis, molecular biology and clinical management of cHCC-CCA to inform current management approaches and outline future paths in precision oncology.

items.title: Inflammatory, Insulinemic, and Plant-Based Dietary Patterns and Diabetes Among Patients with Acute Pancreatitis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the DREAM Study.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Plant-based diets are widely recommended for lowering the risk of type 2 diabetes, with the caveat that their health benefits depend on the quality of the foods consumed. This analysis examined associations between five dietary patterns and pre-existing diabetes among patients with acute pancreatitis (AP), a population in which the relationship between diet and diabetes has not been well characterized. Methods : Participants were drawn from the Diabetes RElated to Acute Pancreatitis and its Mechanisms (DREAM) study, an ongoing multicenter study of adults aged 18 to 75 years with AP in the U.S. This cross-sectional analysis evaluated five dietary patterns using food frequency questionnaires (FFQ): the reverse Empirical Dietary Index for Hyperinsulinemia (rEDIH), the reverse Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Pattern (rEDIP), the overall plant-based diet index (PDI), the healthful plant-based diet index (hPDI), and the unhealthful plant-based diet index (uPDI). We used multivariable logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) for pre-existing diabetes (i.e., prior to the AP episode). Results: A total of 647 participants (mean age 49.1 ± 14.5 years) were included. In multivariable-adjusted analyses, participants in the highest versus lowest tertile of PDI had 55% lower odds of pre-existing diabetes (adjusted OR: 0.45; 95% CI: 0.25-0.80; p -trend = 0.005). No statistically significant associations were detected for rEDIP, rEDIH, hPDI, or uPDI. Conclusions: Higher overall PDI scores were associated with lower odds of prevalent diabetes. Among patients with AP, further studies are needed to evaluate dietary contributions to future diabetes development following AP and identify potential dietary strategies for diabetes prevention.
authors: Type 1 Diabetes in Acute Pancreatitis Consortium (T1DAPC)

items.title: Concordant Metabolite Differences Across Cecal Content, Liver, and Plasma in Mice Fed an Obesogenic Diet Containing Common Bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.): A Multi-Compartment Metabolomics Study.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: How metabolic changes accompanying common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) consumption are organized across gut, liver, and blood, and which are separable from lower adiposity, is unclear. Methods: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed an obesogenic diet with or without cooked bean powder supplying 70% (nominal) of total dietary protein for 14 weeks; diets were assigned to whole cages (4 per diet). Diets were formulated to nominally match macronutrient proportions ( w / w ) from ingredient and supplier values; sources, and hence estimated protein, amino acid, α-linolenate, and fiber supply, differed; intake was not measured. Cecal content, liver, and plasma were profiled by untargeted metabolomics and liver by RNA-seq for selected gene sets. Metabolite classes selected by three-compartment concordance were examined against prior predictions. Results: Diet groups separated in every compartment, most strongly in cecal content. In all three, 36 host metabolites differed concordantly and 22 KEGG pathways were significant. Five classes met the selection criteria: branched-chain amino acids and their keto acids accumulated in cecal content despite lower estimated supply; long-chain n -3 and n -6 fatty acids shifted reciprocally while hepatic Fads2 , Elovl5 , and Fads1 transcripts were 45-61% of control; and glutathione-related metabolites, ceramides, and bile acids differed as predicted. Total depot mass was significantly lower only in the full cohort (-12%). After MANCOVA adjustment for depot redistribution and hepatic lipid, the branched-chain class retained its diet association (q-value = 0.012), the glutathione-related (q-value = 0.047) and n -3 (q-value = 0.049) classes did so provisionally, the former and the hepatic component of the latter depending on one cage in cage-aware models, and ceramides (q-value = 0.20) and bile acids (q-value = 0.15) did not. Conclusions: Whether these differences drive or follow the leaner phenotype requires time-course, single-constituent designs in both sexes.
